Needless to say in Sooraj Devi vs. Pyare Lal, (1981) 1 SCC 500, it was held by the Hon’ble Supreme Court that; “A clerical or arithmetical error is an error occasioned by an accidental slip or omission of the court. error is an error occasioned by an accidental slip or omission of the court. It represents that which the court never intended to say. It is an error apparent on the face of the record and does not depend for its discovery on argument or disputation. An arithmetical error is a mistake of calculation, and a clerical error is a mistake in writing or typing.” In view of the above legal position and facts, it is clear that on account of some computer related issues and mistakes while cut and paste of the names of the accused persons which were being repeatedly mentioned, the above said inadvertent mistakes occurred whereas in the discussion there were proper details about their roles.

plain.1: First day of the case. The Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) filed its criminal complaint and full investigation report against Adarsh Buildestate and others before the Gurugram Sessions Judge acting as Special Court under the Companies Act, with bulky records in four boxes. The court accepted it subject to checking and registration, told the court clerk (Ahlmad) to verify the documents and copies, and noted that besides those already arrested there are 178 more accused to be prosecuted. Adjourned to 24.5.2019 to consider summoning the other accused.
plain.2: Copies of the complaint and full record were handed over to the lawyers for Mukesh Modi and Rahul Modi; Vivek Harivyasi, who is on bail, will get his copy on 30.05.2019. The accused asked for a soft (electronic) copy because the record is huge; the SFIO investigating officer Prashant Baliyan said he would take instructions from his department. SFIO's arguments on summoning were partly heard and the case was adjourned to 28.05.2019.
plain.3: Hearing on whether the court should take up the case and summon the accused. SFIO asked to file a corrected list of accused and witnesses with full addresses, explaining that although it seeks to prosecute about 186 accused, six names were accidentally left out of the original list. The court allowed the correction since it only fixes an inadvertent mistake in the title, and took the amended lists on record. More SFIO arguments were heard; next date 30.05.2019.
plain.4: Vivek Harivyasi was excused from coming to court for the day because he suffered serious medical complications the night before and was admitted to Park Hospital, supported by medical records; he must appear on 01.07.2019. Mukesh Modi and Rahul Modi, in jail, attended by video link and were kept in judicial custody till 13.06.2019. Arguments on summoning the accused finished; order fixed for 03.06.2019. The request for a soft copy of the complaint was refused because SFIO said none can be given.
plain.5: Short order. A new lawyer, Ms. Shreya Dixit, filed her authority (power of attorney) for Vivek Harivyasi and received the copies of the complaint and the full record on his behalf, and her statement was recorded. The file was to be taken up after lunch the same day for the court's order on taking cognizance (formally taking up the case).
plain.6: Short operative order summoning all 187 accused. Finding enough initial evidence, the court listed which companies and people face which charges: cheating and conspiracy, Companies Act fraud (Section 447), criminal breach of trust (Mukesh, Priyanka and Rahul Modi), forgery (the Modis, Vaibhav Lodha, Neha Gemawat, Jainam Rathod and others), illegally taking deposits, false accounts, and auditor offences (Abhay K Shah, S L Bohra & Associates). All are summoned through bailable warrants of Rs 10,000 to appear on 30.07.2019; SFIO must prepare the warrants within 15 days for service through the DCP Gurugram.
plain.7: The detailed order taking up the SFIO complaint and summoning all 187 accused. It summarises the investigation: Mukesh Modi's Adarsh group took over Rs 1700 crore in loans from Adarsh Credit Cooperative Society (outstanding Rs 4120 crore), siphoned cash shown as cash in hand, used fake cloth-purchase bills and false deposit slips after demonetisation, a Noida land deal, the Riddhi Siddhi group, Vivek Harivyasi's companies and Riyasat Green Farm, auditor Abhay K Shah, Rajiv Kumar Rana and Mahesh Dutt Sharma. Finding enough initial evidence, the court framed the list of offences and issued bailable warrants of Rs 10,000 for 30.07.2019.
plain.8: Mukesh Modi and Rahul Modi were not brought from Gurugram jail because Rajasthan Police (Special Operations Group, Jaipur) had taken them to Jaipur in another case, FIR 24 of 2018, without this court's permission. The court issued a show-cause notice to the SOG station officer for not producing them and asked the Gurugram jail superintendent to explain handing them over. Production warrants were issued for the Modis for 17.06.2019 and, for several other accused already jailed in Jaipur, for 01.07.2019. Matter sent to the vacation judge S.K. Duggal.
plain.9: Vacation judge order. SOG Jaipur Inspector Ravinder Kumar brought Mukesh Modi and Rahul Modi to court, explaining they were on police remand in Jaipur till 22.6.2019 and could not be produced on 13.6.2019; he asked that they stay in police custody for the investigation. The Gurugram jail superintendent replied that no deliberate mistake was made in handing them over and regretted the inconvenience. The reply was kept for consideration on 1.7.2019, and the inspector was told to produce the accused that day.
plain.10: Jaipur Police again failed to bring Mukesh Modi and Rahul Modi, with no explanation; a police official said other accused could not be brought for lack of police force. Fresh production warrants were issued for the Modis and others (Ishwar Singh Sindal, Bharat Modi, Vaibhav Lodha, Bharat Das Vaishnav, Rohit Modi, Virender Modi, Vivek Purohit) for 30.07.2019. Priyanka Modi, produced in custody, was kept in judicial custody till 15.07.2019. Vivek Harivyasi applied for bail on the added offences while SFIO asked to cancel his existing bail; his bail was extended till the hearing on 05.07.2019.
plain.11: Short remand order. Priyanka Modi, who was in custody, was brought to court by the jail authorities. SFIO's team (senior standing counsel Lokender Raghav, prosecutor Hari Kishan and investigating officer Prashant Baliyan) asked for her further custody. The court agreed and kept her in judicial custody till 30.07.2019, directing that she be produced again on that date through video conferencing.
plain.12: First appearance date after summoning, dealing with each of the 187 accused. Group companies are to be represented by Rohit Modi, Sidharth Chauhan, Vivek Harivyasi, Surender Singh and others. Many warrants came back unserved and were reissued for 04.09.19 with the complaint. Requests by Paras Bolia, the Tak family, Peeyush Aggarwal and others to be excused from coming to court on medical or personal grounds were rejected as afterthoughts. Jainam Rathod, Raj Kumar Modi, Ramlal Arya and others surrendered and were let out on interim bail of Rs 50,000 and had to deposit passports. Auditors Ichchhita Dungarwal and Neha Kataria got bail because their offences are bailable.
plain.13: Rohit Modi was brought from custody and marked present for the Adarsh group companies. Bail hearings for Surender Singh, Jainam Rathod, Raj Kumar Modi and ten accused directors who say they signed the account books without bad intent were put off to 20.8.2019, with interim bail extended. Bharat Kumar Mardia argued he was not summoned for fraud under Section 447. Raj Kumar Modi was excused from coming that day because he was unwell. The Modis and Vivek Harivyasi stayed in judicial custody, and Vaibhav Lodha, Virender Modi, Rohit Modi and others already held in Jaipur were also taken into custody in this case.
plain.14: Only Vivek Harivyasi was brought (from Bhondsi jail, Gurugram) and was kept in judicial custody till 04.09.2019, to appear by video link. The other ten accused held in Central Jail, Jaipur, including Mukesh Modi, Rahul Modi and Priyanka Modi, were not produced and the jail sent no information; SFIO's counsel said Rahul and Mukesh Modi had perhaps been taken by Gujarat police. Fresh production warrants were issued for 4.9.2019 and the Jaipur jail superintendent was asked to explain why they were not produced.
plain.15: Bail refused. By a separate detailed order, the court dismissed the regular bail applications of Jainam Rathod, Surender Singh, Ajit Singh Rathore, Ram Lal Arya, Hemant Kumar Jain, Praveen Kumar, Damyanti Bhandari, Nimesh Kumar Soni, Rituraj Singh Sisodia, Dushyant Singh Rathore, Shashank Shekhar Singh Rathore and Jitesh Kumar Parmar, who were present in court; they were taken into custody and sent to Bhondsi jail, Gurugram, till 4.9.2019. Bharat Kumar Mardia's application for anticipatory bail (protection from arrest) was also dismissed and an arrest warrant issued against him for 4.9.2019.
plain.16: Raj Kumar Modi's regular bail application was dismissed by a separate detailed order and his interim bail from 13.8.2019 was cancelled. He did not come to court even though he was on interim bail and supposed to appear, and his lawyer gave no explanation. An arrest warrant was issued for 04.09.2019, his bail and surety bonds were forfeited, and his surety was given a notice to explain why action should not be taken for his non-appearance.
plain.17: Long roll-call order. Jaipur jail again failed to bring Rohit Modi, Mukesh Modi, Rahul Modi and others; new production warrants and an explanation were ordered. Sidharth Chauhan, refused anticipatory bail on 1.8.2019, still had not surrendered; arrest warrant sent to the DCP. Raj Kumar Modi stayed absent; notice went to his surety Rekha Modi. Rajeev Verma, Sushil Maloo and Rajendra Singh Bhandari were excused from attending. Abhay K Shah, the Tak family and others got protection from arrest until their anticipatory bail is decided. Arrest warrants were issued against accused found deliberately avoiding service, such as Peeyush Aggarwal and Paras Bolia. Vijay Shukla showed a Supreme Court no-coercive-action order.
plain.18: Short order about Vijay Shukla (A-149), who appeared in person. He filed a copy of the Supreme Court's order of the same day adjourning his writ petition to 12.9.2019 and continuing the interim protection that no coercive action (such as arrest) be taken against him. He was directed to appear in this court on 13.9.2019, subject to the Supreme Court's further directions.
plain.19: Vijay Shukla showed that the Supreme Court had adjourned his case to 19.9.2019 and extended his protection from arrest, so he must appear on 20.9.2019. Separately, the anticipatory bail applications of Shinder Pal Singh and Gurbir Singh Sandhu were dismissed by a detailed order, their temporary protection was withdrawn, and arrest warrants were issued for 03.10.2019 through a special police team with SFIO officials. The landlord of Shinder Pal Singh's rented house in Sector 9-B, Chandigarh had complained that police were deliberately not arresting him, so that address goes on the warrant.
plain.20: Paramvir Singh Sangwan (A-174) asked that his arrest warrant be put on hold because the High Court, in his writ petition (CWP 23904 of 2019), had passed an interim order on 13.09.2019 in the same terms as the Supreme Court's no-coercive-action order for Vijay Shukla. The court accepted this and directed that the arrest warrant issued on 04.09.2019 not be carried out, informing the DCP (HQ) Gurugram. Notice of his application went to SFIO for 27.09.2019.
plain.21: Roll-call order. Central Jail Jaipur again did not send Rohit Modi and nine other jailed accused, claiming a Jaipur magistrate (ACMM) needed them; the court found this baseless, since the ACMM never barred sending them and has no power over this Special Court. Fresh production warrants were issued for 03.10.2019, with copies to the ACMM and the Jaipur SSP to provide police escort. Mukesh Modi, Rahul Modi and Ishwar Singh Sindal were said to be with Ahmedabad police. Arrest warrants were renewed for Sidharth Chauhan and Raj Kumar Modi. Six accused had been granted anticipatory bail (protection from arrest); custody of others extended.
plain.22: Joydeep Das Gupta, Lovekush Sharma, Poonam Madan, Praveen Maheshwari, Rajeev Maheshwari and Avanish Kumar Tyagi, who had been granted anticipatory bail, furnished their bail bonds. The five who work as senior executives asked to be freed from depositing their passports since they must travel often. SFIO's counsel did not dispute that it is basically a case of no evidence against these six, so the court dropped the conditions to hand over passports and not to leave India without permission. Avanish Kumar Tyagi swore an affidavit that he has no passport. All to appear 3.10.2019.
plain.23: Hearing on Vivek Harivyasi's bail, with him present on bail and senior counsel Satish Aggarwal for SFIO. After some argument, both sides relied on new facts and case law against each other and asked for time to study the judgments cited. The case was adjourned to 17.07.2019 for further arguments, and Vivek Harivyasi's existing bail was extended till then on the same terms.
plain.24: Correction order, pronounced 11 July 2019. SFIO pointed out copy-paste (clerical) mistakes in the list of who was summoned for what in the 03.06.2019 summoning order: names of individual accused A-115 to A-141 were missing from the fraud paragraph, company names were missing elsewhere, Virender Modi was left out, Bharat Mardia was wrongly written instead of Bharat Modi, and Shinder Pal Singh, Gurbir Singh Sandhu and Mahesh Dutt Sharma were wrongly included in one paragraph. Relying on a Supreme Court ruling on clerical errors, the court allowed the correction and replaced paragraph 9 with a corrected list.
plain.25: Anticipatory bail (protection from arrest) hearings for twelve accused including Jinendra Vyas, auditor Abhay K Shah, the Tak family, Megha Chauhan, Shyam Bihari Gupta, Sudhir Mehta, Raj Kumar Bohra and Mahesh Dutt Sharma. After two hours of argument for Vyas and Shah, all twelve were adjourned to 23.9.2019 because Mahendra Tak's senior lawyer R.K. Handoo had to go to Ludhiana; their temporary protection was extended. Nitin Rathore's request to cancel his arrest warrant without surrendering, claiming he had moved address 5-6 years ago, was dismissed as a delaying tactic.
plain.26: Vijay Shukla (A-149) appeared and filed the Supreme Court's order of 19.09.2019: his request for interim relief was turned down, but he was allowed to seek anticipatory or regular bail in the proper court, and his protection from arrest was extended for ten days to do so. He had not filed any bail application yet, so he was left free to do so within that time. Next date 03.10.2019.
plain.27: Short adjournment. The case was listed for the court's decision on the anticipatory bail (protection from arrest) applications of auditor Abhay K Shah (CIS No. 3303 of 2019) and Jinender Vyas (CIS No. 3320 of 2019), with their local lawyers present, but the orders were not ready. Put off to 23.9.2019 for orders on both applications.
plain.28: Part arguments heard on anticipatory bail (protection from arrest) applications of the Tak family (Mahesh Kumar, Saurabh, Ravi, Indu, Mahendra Kumar Tak), Raj Kumar Bohra, Sudhir Mehta, Shyam Bihari Gupta, Megha Chauhan, Mahesh Dutt Sharma, Paras Bolia and Shiv Raj Sharma; further hearing on 30.9.2019 since a similar case was pending in the High Court. After lunch, auditor Abhay K Shah's anticipatory bail was dismissed by a detailed order, his temporary protection withdrawn, and, as he had not surrendered, an arrest warrant was issued for 03.10.2019.
plain.29: Jinender (Jinendra) Vyas's anticipatory bail application (protection from arrest) was dismissed by a separate detailed order, and his temporary protection was withdrawn. Because he had not surrendered, an arrest warrant was issued against him for 03.10.2019. The file was also listed for 27.9.2019 on Paramvir Singh Sangwan's request to withdraw his arrest warrant.
plain.30: Paramvir Singh Sangwan's request to withdraw his arrest warrant. His lawyer said the Punjab and Haryana High Court had on 26.9.2019 listed his writ petition for a later date and told this court to decide his bail on merits, though the certified copy had not arrived. Since he has now applied for anticipatory bail, to be heard with similar accused, the court ordered that his arrest warrant not be carried out till 04.10.2019, subject to any High Court directions.
plain.31: Remand order by Additional Sessions Judge A.K. Bishnoi, as the regular judge was on casual leave. Vivek Harivyasi attended through video conferencing. Jainam Rathod, Ajit Singh Rathore, Ram Lal Arya, Hemant Kumar Jain, Praveen Kumar, Damyanti Bhandari, Nimesh Kumar Soni, Rituraj Singh, Dushyant Singh Rathore, Shashank Shekhar Singh Rathore, Jitesh Kumar Parmar, Surender Singh and Priyanka Modi were produced in custody. All were kept in judicial custody till 14.10.2019, to be produced by video conferencing.
plain.32: New Sessions Judge M.M. Dhonchak handled many requests to be excused from coming to court. Aditya Sarda was excused for the day despite an arrest warrant, citing viral fever without a medical certificate; the Maheshwari brothers (out of station on work) and several company representatives (fever, out of station) were also excused for the day. Abhay K Shah's request was refused as his anticipatory bail was already dismissed, and Vimal Sanwarmal Sharma's was refused as the High Court gave him no protection. Vijay Shukla was excused while his anticipatory bail is pending. Non-bailable warrants against Sidharth Chauhan, Peeyush Aggarwal and others were reissued; the Modis came from custody.
plain.33: Short procedural order by Sessions Judge M.M. Dhonchak. Lawyers appeared for many accused with pending bail applications, including Paramvir Singh Sangwan, the Tak family, Shyam Bihari Gupta, Sudhir Mehta, Raj Kumar Bohra, Megha Chauhan, Vijay Shukla, Mahesh Dutt Sharma, Naveen Choudhary, Paras Bolia, Nitin Rathore and Shiv Raj Sharma. The court said separate orders had been passed on the bail applications and need not be repeated. Next date 14.10.2019.
plain.34: Routine custody date. Vivek Harivyasi, Jainam Rathod, Ajit Singh Rathore, Ram Lal Arya, Hemant Kumar Jain, Praveen Kumar, Damyanti Bhandari, Nimesh Kumar Soni, Rituraj Singh, Dushyant Singh Rathore, Shashank Shekhar Singh Rathore, Jitesh Kumar Parmar and Surender Singh were marked present by video conferencing, and Priyanka Modi was brought to court. All are to be produced before the court on 19.10.2019.
plain.35: Roll-call order by Additional Sessions Judge Raj Gupta. Jaipur jail did not bring Rohit Modi, citing too few police, nor the Modis and Priyanka Modi; Bhondsi jail did not bring Vivek Harivyasi, Surender Singh, Jainam Rathod and others, so all were summoned for 2.11.2019. Abhay K Shah's request to be excused while he approaches the High Court was refused. People excused for the day on medical grounds: Praveen and Rajeev Maheshwari (lung infection/bronchitis), Aditya Sarda (viral fever, chest pain), a company representative (diarrhoea). Bharat Kumar Mardia was excused as the High Court extended his pre-arrest bail. Arrest warrants against Jinendra Vyas, Shinder Pal Singh and others were extended.
plain.36: Roll-call order by Judge Raj Gupta. Rohit Modi, Mukesh Modi, Rahul Modi, Priyanka Modi and others were finally brought from Jaipur jail, and Vivek Harivyasi, Surender Singh and Jainam Rathod from Bhondsi, all kept in custody till 22.11.2019. Abhay K Shah's request to be excused was refused as the High Court gave no interim protection. Bharat Kumar Mardia was let out on bail of Rs 50,000 under the High Court's pre-arrest bail order. Excused for the day: Poonam Madan (work at DLF), Praveen Maheshwari (meeting in Chennai for Wheels India), Aditya Sarda (documents not supplied), Vimal Sanwarmal Sharma (viral fever) and Ichchhita Dungarwal (two-year-old child unwell).
plain.37: Pure adjournment. No one appeared; the file was taken up early because 11.11.2019 had been declared a local holiday, and the case was adjourned to a later date (left blank in the order) for the same purpose, with all concerned to be informed. Order by Additional Sessions Judge Raj Gupta.
plain.38: Roll-call order by Judge Raj Gupta. Vivek Harivyasi was not produced as he had been taken to the government hospital, Gurugram, for ill-health. The High Court had refused bail to Sidharth Chauhan, Surender Singh, Jainam Rathod and Raj Kumar Modi. A police constable's salary was ordered attached for falsely reporting that Abhay K Shah was away on a religious trip. Damyanti Bhandari, now on bail, applied to become an approver (witness for the prosecution) under a High Court order; Nimesh Soni and Shashank Shekhar Singh Rathore had similar applications. Joydeep Das Gupta, Poonam Madan, Ichchhita Dungarwal and others were excused from appearing until further orders.
plain.39: Roll-call order by Judge Raj Gupta, mostly by video link; next date 31.1.2020. Rahul Modi, Mukesh Modi and Ishwar Singh Sindal were not produced as they had been taken to courts in Junagarh and Sabarmati. Abhay K Shah and Nitin Rathore were refused excuse from attending as the High Court had given them no protection. Aditya Sarda's request to cancel his arrest warrant was refused; he had been deliberately avoiding service. Rajiv Kumar Rana got temporary protection from arrest pending anticipatory bail. Ajit Singh Rathore, Ramlal Arya, Damyanti Bhandari and other bailed accused are to give statements as approvers (prosecution witnesses) as the High Court directed.
plain.40: Roll-call order by new judge Dr. D.N. Bhardwaj; next date 08.05.2020. Rohit Modi, the Modis, Priyanka Modi, Vivek Harivyasi, Jainam Rathod, Surender Singh and Raj Kumar Modi appeared from jail by video link. Abhay K Shah and Nitin Rathore were refused excuse from coming, as no High Court order protected them. Jai Singh Chauhan, representative of the Riddhi Siddhi companies, was excused for the day for a family wedding. Bharat Kumar Mardia and the Maheshwari brothers were excused until further orders because they live and do business in different parts of India. Fresh arrest warrants went out for Sidharth Chauhan, Jinendra Vyas, Shinder Pal Singh and Gurbir Singh Sandhu.
plain.41: Pure adjournment due to COVID-19. No one appeared. The file was taken up early under an order (Endst. No. 2495 dated 02.05.2020) of the District and Sessions Judge, Gurugram, issued because of the situation arising from the coronavirus (COVID-19) outbreak. The case was adjourned to 24.09.2020 for the same purpose already fixed, and all concerned were to be informed.
plain.42: COVID-19 period hearing fixed for presence of accused; most did not appear, and the case was adjourned to 14.01.2021, with warrants to continue against those without bail or protection. Jailed accused were not produced because video conferencing was not working. Many were excused from attending, including company representatives, Paramvir Singh Sangwan, Leena and Vivek Harivyasi, and the Tak family. Vijay Jindal's request, saying he was being admitted to AIIMS Delhi for treatment, was refused since his anticipatory bail was rejected and the High Court gave no protection. Mahesh Dutt Sharma's High Court protection was extended to 3.11.2020; Vimal Sanwarmal Sharma furnished bail bonds.
plain.43: Short order by Additional Sessions Judge Dr. D.N. Bhardwaj. The file was taken up on the application of accused Raj Kumar Bohra, through his advocate B.S. Motsara, for furnishing bail. His bail bonds and surety bonds were furnished as required by the earlier order dated 11.08.2020 and accepted; after compliance the papers were to be attached to the main case file.
plain.44: Pure adjournment due to COVID-19. No one appeared. The file was taken up under an order (Endst. No. 01 dated 02.01.2021) of the District and Sessions Judge, Gurugram, issued because of the coronavirus (COVID-19) situation. The case was adjourned to 15.01.2021 for the same purpose already fixed, and all concerned were to be informed of the new date.
plain.45: Hearing for presence of accused. Mahesh Kumar Tak (A-187) was reported to have died. Company representatives, Megha Chauhan, Indu Tak, Ravi Tak and Jitesh Kumar Parmar were excused from attending, but Vijay Shukla's request (gone to Chandigarh for his anticipatory bail in the High Court) was refused since he had no protection. Jailed accused, including the Modis, Rohit Modi and Jainam Rathod, were not produced because video conferencing was not connected. Surender Singh was still in Virat Hospital, Rewari, and his lawyer must file his medical records. Approver applications of Ajit Singh Rathore, Ram Lal Arya and others are pending; their statements to be recorded 19.02.2021.
plain.46: The jailed accused (Rohit Modi, Mukesh Modi, Rahul Modi, Priyanka Modi, Jainam Rathod and others) were again not produced because video conferencing was not connected; SFIO's officers joined by WhatsApp. For Surender Singh, who is in hospital, only a medical certificate was filed without treatment records, and his lawyer sought time as his senior was unavailable. The court directed Dr. Virender Yadav or the in-charge of Virat Hospital, Rewari, to produce his treatment record in court through a knowledgeable person by 19.1.2021.
plain.47: Only Jainam Rathod and Raj Kumar Modi were produced from custody by video link; the other jailed accused were not. For Surender Singh, Sandeep, in charge of nursing staff at Virat Hospital, Rewari, produced only an ICU chart from 11.1.2021 and blood reports of 16-18.1.2021 and could not explain his medical condition. He said the treating doctor, who could not join by video, would come with the full record. SFIO did not object, and the case was adjourned to 21.01.2021 for the treating doctor to appear with complete medical records.
plain.48: Dr. Viratveer Yadav of Virat Hospital, Rewari appeared by video and said Surender Singh had COVID-19 and is now on intermittent BiPAP support (a breathing machine) with chest physiotherapy for severe lung fibrosis caused by the coronavirus, but is recovering well and can be moved in 10-15 days. His treatment records did not arrive because hospital staff were stuck in a traffic jam near village Masani due to the farmers' protest (Kisan Andolan). The court ordered him shifted back to Bhondsi jail on 1.2.2021 and allowed SFIO to have a Medical Board verify his condition and treatment.
plain.49: Only Jainam Rathod and Surender Singh were produced from custody by video link; the others were not as the video link was not connected, and Raj Kumar Modi was said to be in Civil Hospital, Gurugram. The court corrected the 15.1.2021 order to record that Shashank Shekhar Singh Rathore, Nimesh Kumar Soni and Damyanti Bhandari had in fact been present. Vijay Shukla filed a High Court order of 28.1.2021 (CRM 24870 of 2020) barring coercive action against him, so no action is to be taken against him on the non-bailable warrant.
plain.50: Hearing for presence of accused. Mahendra Kumar Tak (A-155) was reported dead, in addition to Mahesh Kumar Tak (A-187); death reports were called from police. Padmawati Art Creation appeared through its representative Fateh Singh. Paramvir Singh Sangwan, aged 74 with old-age illnesses and at high COVID-19 risk, was excused from attending until further orders. Vijay Shukla keeps High Court protection. The Modis and others were not produced because Rajasthan Police had taken them on police remand. Statements of accused who want to become approvers (witnesses for the prosecution), such as Ajit Singh Rathore, Ram Lal Arya and Damyanti Bhandari, were scheduled from 5.3.2021 to 30.4.2021.
plain.51: Lawyer Joydeep Bhattacharya explained that at the previous hearing on 19 Feb 2021 he had actually been present for Ichhita Dundarwal (A-180) and Neha Kataria (A-181), who are already permanently excused from coming to court, but forgot to sign the attendance sheet. The court accepted this, marked both women as present through their lawyer, and cancelled the fresh court notice that would otherwise have been sent to them. Case kept for 7 May 2021.
plain.52: Ram Lal Arya and Ajit Singh Rathore, who want to switch sides and become witnesses for the prosecution in return for a pardon (approvers), came to court, but their statements were not recorded because SFIO's lawyer asked for more time since the investigating officer was absent and had to study their proposed statements. Their recording was put off till 7 May 2021. Raj Kumar Modi, Surender, Jainam Rathore and Vijay Jindal were shown by video link from jail; other jailed accused held in Jodhpur Jail were not produced, so production orders were issued.
plain.53: Mostly a jail-production hearing. Raj Kumar Modi and Jainam Rathore appeared from jail by video link and Surender was brought to court by jail staff. Vijay Jhindal could not appear because he was admitted in the General Hospital, Gurugram; he is to be shown by video from hospital if possible. Other jailed accused said to be in Jodhpur Jail were again not produced, so fresh production orders were issued and the Jodhpur Jail Superintendent was asked to explain why (show cause notice). Next date 2 April 2021.
plain.54: Several jailed accused were not brought to court. Rajasthan police said Priyanka Modi, Rajeshwar Singh, Vaibhav Lodha, Bharat Das Vaishnav, Rohit Modi, Bharat Modi, Vivek Purohit, Virender Modi and Ishwar Singh Sindal were in police custody (remand) in a Jaipur case (FIR 218/2019, Vidhayakpuri), and Mukesh Kumar Modi and Rahul Virender Modi were on remand in a Jodhpur case (FIR 136/2021). The court asked the Jaipur Jail Superintendent for a detailed explanation, issued a fresh warning notice to the Jodhpur Jail Superintendent for not replying, and ordered production on 16 April 2021. A hospital report on Vijay Jhindal (admitted in General Hospital, Gurugram) was called from the CMO.
plain.55: New judge Phalit Sharma received the case by transfer. Jaipur jail produced Vaibhav, Rohit Modi, Bharat Modi, Rajeshwar Singh, Ishwar Singh, Bharat Dass, Priyanka and Vivek Purohit. Jodhpur jail said Rahul and Mukesh Modi could not be brought because no police escort was available, and apologised. Virender Modi was not produced because jail said he was on interim bail till 17 April 2021, but this court never gave him bail, so the court asked Jodhpur jail to explain why he was let out and ordered all to appear by video on 30 April 2021. Surender was not produced from Bhondsi Jail.
plain.56: Roll-call of jailed accused by video link. Priyanka Modi (women's jail, Jaipur), Rajeshwar, Bharat Modi, Ishwar Singh, Rohit Modi, Vaibhav, Bharat and Vivek Purohit (Central Jail Jaipur) and Vaibhav and Raj Kumar Modi (Bhondsi Jail, Gurugram) appeared by video and were kept in judicial custody. Rahul and Mukesh were not produced from Jodhpur jail and Surender was not produced by Jaipur jail authorities, so production orders were issued. Virender Modi was absent, being on interim bail from the High Court. Next date 20 May 2021.
plain.57: Short adjournment order with nobody present. The file was taken up on the instructions of the District and Sessions Judge, Gurugram (order of 13 May 2021), as the matter was routine in nature. The case was postponed to 8 September 2021 for the purpose already fixed and parties were to be informed. The judge explained the long gap was due to the heavy load of very old cases in his recently joined court that need priority.
plain.58: SFIO asked the court to split off and separately try the accused who had not yet been served (under sections 299/317 CrPC). The court rejected this, saying there was no proof those accused had run away and SFIO seemed to be avoiding its own job of getting them arrested with police help. The judge also scolded court staff and SFIO for not telling him those accused had been summoned, ordered bailable warrants (Rs 5,000 each with one surety) as earlier directed on 19 Feb 2021, and asked police for death reports of Mahender Kumar Tak and Mahesh Kumar Tak.
plain.59: Correction to the same day's order. Because an earlier order of 4 Sep 2019 had already directed arrest, the court ordered arrest warrants (not bailable warrants, which had not worked) against Nitin Rathore, Vinay Kumpawat, Paras Bolia, Manish Chauhary, Deepak Shrimali, Prakash Chandra Purohit, Akshat Singh, Naveen Kumar, Aditya Sarda, Sudhir Punia, Shiv Raj Sharma, Naveen Choudhary, Peeyush Aggarwal, Rajiv Kumar Rana and Sidharth Chauhan, and also against Jinender Vyas, Abhay K. Shah, Shinder Pal Singh, Gurbir Singh Sandhu, Shyam Bihari Gupta, Sudhir Mehta and Saurabh Tak. Vijay Shukla, Nazima Khan and Shabir Khan to be called through bailable warrants.
plain.60: Raj Kumar Modi was let out of jail on interim bail after the Supreme Court (order of 16 Aug 2021, following the interim bail given to main accused Vivek Harivyasi) allowed it. Conditions: personal bond of Rs 1 lakh with one surety, no foreign travel without permission, surrender passport, no similar business, no tampering with evidence, share phone number and location with SFIO. His wife Rekha Modi stood surety using two ICICI Bank fixed deposits of Rs 50,000 each, which the court kept and informed the bank. Release order sent to jail.
plain.61: Brief adjournment order. Nobody appeared on behalf of the complainant SFIO on this date, and no decision was taken. The judge simply directed that the file be put up on 8 September 2021, the date already fixed in the main case, when the accused were due to appear. Nothing else happened at this hearing.
plain.62: Big roll-call hearing. Customs intelligence (DRI) sought permission to question jailed Jainam Rathore. Mahesh Dutt Sharma excused for today due to a High Court no-arrest assurance; Abhay K. Shah's request to be excused rejected as he never surrendered. Vijay Shukla appeared under Supreme Court no-arrest protection. Ten accused who became approvers (prosecution witnesses for pardon) to give statements, starting with Ajit Singh and Ram Lal Arya on 17 Sep 2021. Arrest warrants for Nazima Khan and Shabbir Khan for dodging; fresh arrest warrants for about 22 others, with absconding proceedings to be considered. Surender in hospital; Vijay Kumar Jhindal reported dead.
plain.63: Short adjournment order. Only SFIO's senior public prosecutor Hari Kishan was present. At his request, the case was postponed to 15 September 2021 for arguments on an application filed by DRI (the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence, a customs and revenue investigation agency). No other decision was taken on this date.
plain.64: Brief cover order on Sudhir Mehta's application in the SFIO case. His lawyer Neeraj Dev Gaur and SFIO's prosecutors were present. SFIO filed its reply, arguments were heard, and the court dismissed Sudhir Mehta's application by a separate detailed order passed the same day (his request to cancel the arrest warrant against him). Papers were attached to the main case file and the order was pronounced in open court.
plain.65: Sudhir Mehta (A-170) of Udaipur asked the court to cancel the arrest warrant against him, citing Supreme Court rulings (Aman Preet Singh, Siddharth) that arrest is not always needed. SFIO argued he had hidden the fact that his anticipatory bail plea was still pending in the High Court and that the Companies Act, a special law, applies. The court rejected his request, mainly because he concealed the pending High Court case (fixed for 1 Nov 2021), and because without a High Court stay on arrest it could not interfere. Arrest warrant stays.
plain.66: Short adjournment order. Only the senior special public prosecutor Satish Aggarwala, appearing for DRI (the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence, a customs and revenue investigation agency) officer Shailendra Singh Bhadauria, was present. At his request, DRI's application was listed for arguments on 17 September 2021. No decision was taken on this date.
plain.67: Raj Kumar Bohra (A-171), a chartered accountant and NRI whose wife (suffering severe depression) and children live in Dubai, asked for general permission to travel abroad. He had travelled to UAE, Bangladesh and Dubai earlier with permission and always returned on time. SFIO opposed only half-heartedly. The court allowed him to travel to UAE from 14 Sep 2021 and return before 23 Dec 2021, on condition he gives property or bank guarantee security of Rs 1 crore (forfeited if he misuses it) and follows his travel plan.
plain.68: Short adjournment on Rajeev Kumar Rana's (A-177) application to cancel the non-bailable arrest warrant against him and to be excused from appearing in court in person. SFIO's prosecutors filed their reply to the application. His lawyers Ajit Sharma and Aakash Jangra asked for time to argue, which the court allowed. The case was fixed for arguments on 22 September 2021.
plain.69: Customs intelligence (DRI) was allowed to question accused Jainam Madhukant Rathod alias Jainam Jain, in jail since 28 Aug 2019, in its separate customs-duty evasion probe involving M/s Shivani Network. The court directed Bhondsi District Jail, Gurugram to let Senior Intelligence Officer Shailendra Singh Bhadauria and officers Ishu Kumar Verma and Anirudh Singh Bhati visit on 21 Sep 2021 with their files to record his statement under section 108 of the Customs Act.
plain.70: Ajit Singh (A-150) and Ram Lal Arya (A-158) came to court to give their statements about becoming approvers (switching sides to be prosecution witnesses in return for a pardon), but the court ran out of time. Their statements were postponed to 14 October 2021 and both were told to appear in person.
plain.71: Brief order on Rajeev Kumar Rana's (A-177) application to cancel the non-bailable arrest warrant against him and be excused from appearing in court in person. His lawyers Ajit Sharma and Aakash Jangra and SFIO's prosecutors argued the matter. The court dismissed the application by a separate detailed order the same day, so the arrest warrant against him stays. Papers attached to the main file.
plain.72: Detailed ruling rejecting Rajeev Kumar Rana's (A-177) request to cancel his non-bailable arrest warrant and excuse him from appearing. He argued that since SFIO never arrested him during the investigation, which he cooperated with, Supreme Court rulings (Siddharth, Aman Preet Singh) mean he should not be arrested now. The court held that fraud under the Companies Act is a special law with strict bail conditions (section 212(6)), relying on High Court rulings in Jainam Rathod and Vijay Shukla cases, and called the request a disguised attempt to get bail. His anticipatory bail had earlier been refused. Arrest warrant stays.
plain.73: Ajit Singh (A-150) and Ram Lal Arya (A-158) again came to court to give their statements about becoming approvers (switching sides to be prosecution witnesses in return for a pardon), but the judge was on half-day casual leave and no court time was left. Their statements were put off to 23 December 2021, the date already fixed in the case, and both were told to come in person.
plain.74: Surender Singh was let out of jail on interim bail after the Supreme Court (order of 29 Oct 2021) noted he became director seven years after the company took the loan, co-accused already had interim bail, and he had been in jail since 2019. Conditions: Rs 1 lakh personal bond and surety, no foreign travel without permission, no similar business, no tampering with evidence, share phone and location with SFIO. His surety deposited Rs 1 lakh cash, to be swapped for a fixed deposit. Jail told not to release him until he deposits his passport with the Supreme Court registry.
plain.75: Short adjournment order with nobody present. Because the judge was going to be on casual leave from 20 to 23 December 2021, the case was taken up early, on 15 December 2021, and postponed to 25 March 2022 for the same purpose already fixed. All concerned were to be informed of the new date. No other decision was taken.
plain.76: Priyanka Modi was let out on bail after the Supreme Court ordered her release on 7 Feb 2022 (Criminal Appeal arising from SLP 301 of 2022), which court staff confirmed. She furnished a personal bond of Rs 1 lakh with one surety, and a release order was issued to the jail. A fixed deposit given as surety was frozen: the State Bank of India branch at Bhagat Ki Kothi, Krishi Upaj Mandi, Jodhpur was told not to cash it without court permission. Next date 6 April 2022.
plain.77: 24 wanted accused to be declared absconding; notices put up publicly (they become 'proclaimed persons' if absent on 2 July 2022) against Nitin Rathore, Jinender Vyas, Vinay Kumpawat, Paras Bolia, Abhay K. Shah, Manish Chaudhary, Deepak Shrimali, Prakash Chandra Purohit, Sidharth Chauhan, Akshat Singh, Shinder Pal Singh, Gurbir Singh Sandhu, Naveen Kumar, Aditya Sarda, Sudhir Punia, Nazima Khan, Shabir Khan, Shiv Raj Sharma, Naveen Chaudhary, Shyam Bihari Gupta, Sudhir Mehta, Saurabh Tak, Peeyush Aggarwal and Rajeev Kumar Rana after warrants since 2019 failed. Cases of dead accused Mahender Kumar Tak and Vijay Kumar Jindal closed. Warrants for Mahesh Kumar Tak; arrest warrants for Neha Gemawat and Meenakshi Modi.
plain.78: Approver statements recorded. Ten accused granted bail by the High Court on condition they cooperate as approvers (switching sides to become prosecution witnesses in return for a pardon) came to court. The statements on oath of Hemant Kumar, Ajit Singh Rathore, Smt. Damyanti and Ram Lal Arya were recorded and the court allowed these four to become approvers. Because court time ran out, the remaining six (Jitesh Kumar, Shashank Shekhar, Dushyant Singh, Nimesh Kumar Soni, Parveen Kumar, Ritu Raj Singh) were called for 7 May 2022.
plain.79: Jainam Rathod (Jainum Rathore) was let out of jail on bail after the Supreme Court ordered his release on 18 April 2022 (Criminal Appeal 640 of 2022). Link Judge Jasbir Singh handled it as the regular judge was on leave. He furnished a personal bond of Rs 1 lakh with one surety and a release order was sent to the jail. The surety's fixed deposit was frozen, with Bank of India, Connaught Circus branch told not to cash it without court permission. Next date 7 May 2022.
plain.80: On SFIO's request, the court ordered that Rajeev Kumar Rana (A-177), a wanted accused against whom proceedings to declare him absconding were under way, be brought from District Jail, Jaipur, where he is held. The Jaipur jail superintendent was directed to produce him by video link if possible on 7 May 2022, or otherwise in person in custody, so that he can be taken into custody in this case in which he had been wanted for a long time.
plain.81: Police officers who served the public 'wanted' proclamation notices gave statements confirming publication against about 22 absconding accused, including Gurbir Singh Sandhu, Shinder Pal Singh, Sidharth Chauhan, Nitin Rathore, Sudhir Mehta, Nazima Khan and Shabbir Khan; they must appear on 2 July 2022. Rajiv Kumar Rana was reported to be in custody in Jaipur, so a production order was issued. The officer for Akshat Singh did not come. Aditya Sharda's request to be excused and Nitin Rathore's request to stop the absconding proceedings were both rejected. Approver Dushyant Singh Rathore's statement was recorded; other approvers' statements postponed.
plain.82: Short procedural order. SFIO applied for a public proclamation (absconding notice) to be issued against accused Akshat Singh. The court received a report from its own clerk (Ahlmad) and called for a report from the clerk of Judge Phalit Sharma's court, which had earlier handled the case, for 11 May 2022.
plain.83: The court found that the proclamation (public 'wanted' notice) against Akshat Singh (A-136), ordered on 25 March 2022, was never actually issued because court constable Ct. Satish Kumar, attached to Judge Phalit Sharma's court, withheld or destroyed the notice given to him on 30 April 2022. A fresh proclamation was ordered, to be published by 25 May 2022, with the constable who serves it to testify on 30 May. Since the matter was already sent to the Gurugram Police Commissioner for inquiry, the court took no further action but asked that the inquiry finish within three months.
plain.84: Short hearing. The public proclamation (absconding notice) against Akshat Singh (A-136) had been put up and the report was filed. But the serving officer, EHC Gajraj, did not appear to give his statement because he fell ill and went to Civil Hospital, Gurugram; a copy of his prescription was placed on record. Case put up on 2 June 2022 for his statement.
plain.85: New judge Dr. Virender Parshad received the case by transfer. EHC Gajraj, the officer who served the absconding notice against Akshat Singh, again did not appear due to his treatment, so the matter was adjourned to 7 June 2022. Meenakshi Modi and Neha Ghemawat Modi asked that arrest warrants not be issued because the Supreme Court had on 20 May 2022 stayed the Rajasthan High Court's order. The court agreed: no arrest warrants against them, and any already issued to be recalled unexecuted.
plain.86: EHC Gajraj Singh, the police officer who put up the public proclamation (absconding notice) against Akshat Singh (A-136), gave his statement confirming it was affixed. Later the same day Akshat Singh's lawyer, Amol Gupta, filed an application asking the court to drop or pause the absconding proceedings against him. A copy was given to SFIO and the case was fixed for 2 July 2022 for the accused's presence and for SFIO's reply on that application.
plain.87: Big roll-call hearing under new judge Dr. Virender Parshad. Absconding proceedings against most of the 24 wanted accused (e.g. Nitin Rathore, Abhay K. Shah, Jinender Vyas, Sudhir Mehta, Rajiv Kumar Rana) were paused till 30 Aug 2022 on High Court orders; also paused for Akshat Singh, Naveen Kumar and Shiv Raj Sharma (who seeks to become an approver). Vinay Kumawat, Sidharth Chauhan and Sudhir Punia did not appear despite proclamation; decision deferred to 27 July. Raj Kumar Bohra sought foreign travel; Megha Chauhan sought her passport back to renew her child's passport. Mahesh Kumar Tak's arrest warrant reissued.
plain.88: Megha Chauhan asked for her passport, kept in the court record, to be returned so she could show it to the passport office to renew the passport of her minor child, Yashas. SFIO did not file a reply but asked that she return it within a fixed time. The court found the reason genuine and released the passport on a Rs 50,000 personal bond with one surety, on condition she returns it within one month, files a certified copy first, and does not leave India without the court's permission.
plain.89: Raj Kumar Bohra, an NRI whose wife (suffering severe depression) and three children live in Dubai and who runs RKC International General Trading LLC in UAE with export business in Bangladesh, asked permission to travel abroad. SFIO gave no objection. Noting he had travelled abroad with permission before and always returned, the court allowed him to travel after 3 July 2022 and come back before 30 Aug 2022, on condition he gives Rs 1 crore security by property or bank guarantee (forfeited if misused) and follows his itinerary.
plain.90: Short order. Naveen Kumar, who had been granted bail by this court on 19 July 2022 in bail application BA-4346-2022, filed his bail bonds through his lawyer Abhimanyu Dhawan. The court accepted and attested the bonds, attached the papers to the main case file, and kept the case for 27 July 2022, the date and purpose already fixed.
plain.91: First page only of the 27 July 2022 hearing, listing attendance. Approvers on bail, including Ajit Singh Rathore, Ramlal Arya, Parveen Kumar, Nimesh Kumar Ramesh Soni, Ritu Raj Singh, Shashank and Dushyant Singh Rathore, Jitesh Kumar Parmar and Damyanti Bhandari, appeared in person. Hemant Kumar Jain, Akshat Singh, Shiv Raj Sharma and Naveen Kumar were represented by lawyers. Mukesh Modi (moved to Hanumangarh jail) and others moved to Jodhpur jail were not produced by Jaipur jail, and Mahesh Kumar Tak was absent.
plain.92: Vinay Kumawat and Sudhir Punia were formally declared 'proclaimed persons' (officially absconding) after failing to appear despite public notices; police and DCP Gurugram told to act against them under section 174-A IPC. Sidharth Chauhan's declaration was postponed because his High Court petition is pending, and Shiv Raj Sharma's paused pending his High Court plea to become an approver. Peeyush Aggarwal's wife Anupama said he would surrender within a week, so he was given time. Akshat Singh and Naveen Kumar had got bail. Rajiv Kumar Rana, shown by video from Jaipur jail, was taken into custody in this case.
plain.93: Short adjournment order. Because the case has 187 accused represented by many lawyers, checking and uploading the detailed order of the day would take time, so by this short order the case was adjourned to 18 October 2022 and 29 November 2022. No other decisions are recorded in this short order.
plain.94: Raj Kumar Bohra, an NRI whose wife (suffering severe depression) and three children live in Dubai, and who runs a trading business in UAE with exports to Bangladesh, was again allowed to travel abroad after 30 Aug 2022 and must return before 18 Oct 2022. SFIO gave no objection. Conditions: Rs 1 crore security by property or bank guarantee (forfeited if misused) and strict travel itinerary. His surety Ajay Kumar Arora, who had already given Rs 1 crore security, agreed by affidavit to continue and to produce him on the next date.
plain.95: Detailed roll-call hearing. Rajiv Kumar Rana appeared by video and stays in custody; Mukesh Modi now moved to Barmer jail. Vinay Kumawat and Sudhir Punia already declared absconding with action under section 174-A. Absconding proceedings against Sidharth Chauhan, Nitin Rathore, Abhay K. Shah and about 17 others stay paused on High Court orders. Peeyush Aggarwal's proclamation put on hold because he filed anticipatory bail. Several accused excused for the day, including Aditya Sarda, Megha Chauhan, Indu Tak and Shiv Raj Sharma. Neha Kataria sought permanent exemption; Meenakshi Modi and Neha Ghemawat Modi sought exemption pending Rajasthan High Court case. Approver statements set for 18 Oct 2022.
plain.96: Short adjournment order. Because the case has 187 accused represented by many lawyers, checking and uploading the detailed order of the day would take time, so by this short order the case was adjourned to 9 December 2022, the date already fixed. No other decisions are recorded in this short order.
plain.97: Raj Kumar Bohra, an NRI whose wife (suffering severe depression) and three children live in Dubai and who runs RKC International General Trading LLC in UAE with exports to Bangladesh, was again allowed to travel abroad after 18 Oct 2022 and must return before 9 Dec 2022. SFIO gave no objection. Conditions: Rs 1 crore security by property or bank guarantee (forfeited if misused) and strict travel itinerary. Surety Ajay Kumar Arora, who already gave Rs 1 crore security, agreed to continue and produce him, and his statement was recorded separately.
plain.98: Detailed roll-call hearing. Rajiv Kumar Rana could not be shown by video because the video link had a technical fault; Mahesh Kumar Tak's arrest warrant came back unserved, so a fresh one was issued with a note that the serving officer must explain any failure. Approver statements postponed to 9 Dec 2022. Absconding proceedings against Sidharth Chauhan and about 18 others remain paused on High Court orders. Shiv Raj Sharma's request to appear only through his lawyer was rejected since his anticipatory bail and approver plea had failed. Several accused excused for the day.
plain.99: Short adjournment order. Because the case has 187 accused represented by many lawyers, checking and uploading the detailed order of the day would take time, so by this short order the case was adjourned to 8 February 2023, the date already fixed. No other decisions are recorded in this short order.
plain.100: Detailed roll-call hearing. Rajiv Kumar Rana again not shown by video due to a technical fault. No coercive action against Mahesh Kumar Tak or Shiv Raj Sharma since their bail applications are now pending in this court. The High Court refused Piyush (Peeyush) Aggarwal's anticipatory bail on 8 Dec 2022 and told him to surrender within a week, so the court will wait for him. Priyanka Modi excused on medical grounds; Ajit Singh, Megha, Damyanti Bhandari, Indu Tak, Raj Kumar Bohra and Ichita also excused. Absconding proceedings against Sidharth Chauhan and others stay paused on High Court orders. Approver statements set for 8 Feb 2023.
plain.101: Short holding order dated 8 February 2023. Because the case has 187 accused and many lawyers, the full detailed order for the day needed time to be checked and uploaded, so the judge simply put the case off to 3 April 2023, the date already fixed. Nothing else was decided in this note; it is a routine adjournment.
plain.102: Detailed hearing order of February 2023 recording attendance of the accused. Accused Virender Modi (122) was reported dead, so a death report was called from the police. Jailed accused were not produced: Mukesh Modi had been moved to Barmer jail, others to Jodhpur jail, and video link for Rajiv Kumar Rana failed, so fresh production warrants issued. A fresh arrest warrant was issued for Mahesh Kumar Tak by special messenger. Accused who agreed to turn prosecution witness for bail (approvers) were told to come to record statements. Proceedings to declare several accused absconding were kept pending High Court orders; five accused excused from attending that day.
plain.103: Short holding order dated 3 April 2023. Since there are 187 accused represented by many lawyers and the full detailed order needed time to be checked and uploaded, the case was simply put off to 22 May 2023 and 30 May 2023, the dates already fixed. A routine adjournment note with no other decision.
plain.104: Detailed hearing of 3 April 2023. Twelve accused, including Nitin Rathore, Saurabh Tak, Sudhir Mehta, Abhay K. Shah, Paras Bolia, Nazima and Shabbir Khan, appeared after the High Court granted them bail, gave bail bonds of Rs 1 lakh each, and the proceedings to declare them absconding were dropped. Naveen Choudhary, Shinder Pal Singh and Gurbir Singh Sandhu did not appear as the High Court had directed, so notices were issued. Shivraj Sharma filed a second request for pardon in exchange for becoming a prosecution witness. The company authorised representative for Goldline International Finvest was replaced. No arrest action against Mahesh Kumar Tak while his anticipatory bail is pending.
plain.105: Order of 19 May 2023: accused Bharat Das Vaishnav (No. 142), who has been in jail in Jaipur since May 2019 in other cases including an SOG Rajasthan FIR, was let out on bail in this case following a High Court order of 12 April 2023. He gave bail and surety bonds of Rs 1 lakh; a vehicle was offered as surety. The court ordered Jaipur jail to release him unless needed in another case, and sent the release order by email.
plain.106: Order of 19 May 2023: accused Vaibhav Lodha (No. 120), held in jail in Jaipur since May 2019 in other cases including an SOG Rajasthan FIR, was let out on bail in this case as directed by the High Court order of 12 April 2023. He furnished bail and surety bonds of Rs 1 lakh, with a vehicle given as surety. Jaipur jail was told to release him unless wanted in another case, and the release order was sent by email.
plain.107: Order of 19 May 2023: accused Bharat Modi (No. 126), in jail in Jaipur since May 2019 in other cases including an SOG Rajasthan FIR, was let out on bail in this case in compliance with a High Court order of 12 April 2023. His bail and surety bonds of Rs 1 lakh were accepted, with a vehicle pledged as surety. Jaipur jail was directed to release him if not required in another case; release order sent by email.
plain.108: Order of 19 May 2023: accused Rohit Modi (No. 123), in custody in Jaipur since May 2019 in other cases including an SOG Rajasthan FIR, was let out on bail in this case after the High Court allowed his petition on 12 April 2023. Bail and surety bonds of Rs 1 lakh were accepted, with a vehicle given as surety. Jaipur jail was ordered to release him unless needed in another case, and the release order was emailed.
plain.109: Order of 22 May 2023 allowing accused Shashank Shekhar Singh Rathore to switch sides and become a witness for the prosecution in return for a pardon (approver), as the High Court had permitted when granting him bail in 2019. The SFIO prosecutor did not object if he tells the truth. He told the judge he would fully and truly disclose everything he knows about the crime and everyone involved. The court warned he would be prosecuted and could be taken into custody if he backs out or stops cooperating. His statement was recorded and kept in a sealed envelope.
plain.110: Short holding order dated 30 May 2023. With 187 accused and many lawyers, the detailed order for the day needed time to be checked and uploaded, so the case was put off to 1 June 2023 and 29 August 2023, the dates already fixed. Routine adjournment note only; nothing else was decided in this short order.
plain.111: Detailed hearing of 30 May 2023. Naveen Choudhary, Gurbir Singh Sandhu and Aditya Sarda appeared and gave bail bonds of Rs 1 lakh each as the High Court had ordered. Shinder Pal Singh still had not turned up, so a final-chance notice was issued. The court noted that five accused who agreed to become prosecution witnesses (approvers) had given statements on 22 May 2023. Meenakshi Modi and Neha Ghemawat Modi said the Supreme Court had barred any arrest or coercive action and promised to appear. Death report of Virender Modi was still awaited; Shivraj Sharma's pardon request adjourned; several accused excused from attending that day.
plain.112: Hearing of 29 August 2023 before Judge Jasbir Singh, mostly roll-call and adjournment to 17 November 2023. Death report of deceased accused Virender Modi still not filed. Jailed accused from Barmer and Jodhpur jails, including Paras Bolia, again not produced, so fresh production warrants issued. SFIO had not replied to Shivraj Sharma's request for pardon to become a prosecution witness. Shinder Pal Singh was given a last-chance notice to appear and furnish bail bonds. Priyanka Modi, Nazima Khan, Ravi Tak, Naveen Chaudhary and three companies were excused from attending that day.
plain.113: Order of 26 September 2023 for accused Megha Chauhan (Tak), No. 163. She had already been allowed on 29 August 2023 to travel abroad, but that permission only works if she gets her passport back. The court clarified that the travel permission includes returning her passport, ordered it released on the earlier conditions, and directed her to hand it back to court within two months of release. Her lawyer must first file a certified copy of the passport.
plain.114: Order of 26 September 2023 for accused Indu Tak, No. 164. She had been allowed on 29 August 2023 to travel abroad, but could not go without her passport. The court corrected the earlier order to say the travel permission includes giving back her passport, ordered it released on the same conditions, and told her to return the passport to court within two months of getting it. Her lawyer must place a certified copy of the passport on record first.
plain.115: Two orders of 30 September 2023 for accused Indu Tak (No. 164) and Megha Chauhan (No. 163), both represented by advocate Bhim Singh Motsara. Following the earlier permission to travel abroad and the order to return their passports, each furnished the required surety bonds, which the court accepted and attested. The court clerk (Ahlmad) was directed to release their passports to them as per rules.
plain.116: Order dated 16 November 2023: no one present. The judge, Jasbir Singh, was going to be on casual leave on 17 November 2023, so the case was simply adjourned to 9 February 2024 for the same purpose, and all parties and their lawyers were to be informed. Routine adjournment only; nothing else decided.
plain.117: Hearing of 9 February 2024 before Judge Roopam. Accused Shinder Pal Singh (137) never appeared despite the High Court's direction, and repeated notices came back unserved, so the court ordered him declared wanted through a public proclamation (Section 82), to be put up by 20 March 2024, with the constable to report on 1 April 2024. Bailable warrants were issued for Priyanka Modi and for absent companies SEARS Built, Alba Polymers, Padamawati Art Creation and Vishal Digital Studio. Death report of Virender Modi still not filed; Shivraj Sharma's pardon request still awaiting SFIO reply; many accused excused from attending that day.
plain.118: Short order of 1 April 2024 before Judge Roopam. The police constable (ASI Sunil Kumar) who was told to publicly put up the proclamation declaring accused Shinder Pal Singh (A-137) wanted/absconding came to court and his statement about publishing it was recorded. Case adjourned to 3 May 2024, the date already fixed, for the appearance of Shinder Pal Singh.
plain.119: Hearing of 3 May 2024 before Judge Roopam. Shinder Pal Singh (137) still did not show up after the 30-day public proclamation period, so he was formally declared a proclaimed offender (absconding/wanted) and police informed. SFIO did not object to Shivraj Sharma's request for a pardon to become a prosecution witness, so it was allowed and he must come to give his statement. Thirteen accused were permanently excused from attending court; Raj Kumar Bohra's exemption requires him to report monthly at the Indian Embassy in Dubai and seek permission before visiting other countries. Bailable warrants for Priyanka Modi and Padmawati Art Creation came back unserved.
plain.120: Order of 3 May 2024 allowing accused Raj Kumar Bohra to travel abroad. He said he is an NRI whose wife Nita Bohra, who suffers from severe depression, and three children live in Dubai, UAE; he is managing partner of RKC International General Trading LLC and travels to UAE and Bangladesh for export business. SFIO opposed orally. Since he had travelled and returned on time on earlier permissions, the court allowed travel after 3 May 2024 on condition of security of property or bank guarantee worth Rs 1 crore, forfeitable if misused. Surety Ajay Kumar Arora agreed to continue.
plain.121: Order of 4 June 2024 before Judge Jagdeep Singh. Accused Jainam Rathod came in person and handed his passport back to the court after it had been released to him. The court took the passport on record and ordered release of his Rs 2 lakh fixed deposit (FDR) that he had given as security when getting the passport, after a photocopy is kept on file. File to be put up on 29 July 2024.
plain.122: Hearing of 29 July 2024 before Judge Jagdeep Singh, mainly attendance and adjournment to 3 September 2024. SFIO was told to file the death report of accused Virender Modi by then. Jailed accused, and those on bail here but held in other cases, to be produced by video link. Thirteen accused excused for that day only but warned to attend next time. Neha Ghemawat and Meenakshi Modi, who had promised to appear, instead filed a bond application; they must produce any higher court stay order or appear in person. Siddharth Chauhan told to file the High Court order protecting him. Priyanka Modi and Prakash Chander Purohit sought permanent exemption.
plain.123: Hearing of 3 September 2024 before Judge Jagdeep Singh. The prosecutor pointed out that ten accused (Ajit Singh Rathore, Ramlal Arya, Hemant Kumar Jain, Parveen Kumar, Damyanti Bhandari, Nimesh Soni, Rituraj Singh, Dushyant Singh Rathore, Shashank Shekhar Singh Rathore, Jitesh Parmar) had already switched sides as prosecution witnesses in return for a pardon (approvers), so the court ordered SFIO to move them to its witness list; they need not attend otherwise. Shiv Raj Sharma's statement may be recorded before a Duty Magistrate. Neha Ghemawat, Meenakshi Modi and Siddharth Chauhan got a last chance to show protective orders or face action for avoiding court.
plain.124: Hearing of 13 November 2024 before Judge Jagdeep Singh. SFIO filed the death certificate of accused Virender Modi showing he died on 18 May 2022, so the case against him was closed (abated). SFIO was told to file an amended case title listing pardoned accused as prosecution witnesses. Shiv Raj Sharma had failed to go before the Duty Magistrate for his approver statement but was said to be ready. Neha Ghemawat and Meenakshi Modi, who still had not appeared or shown any protective order, and Siddharth Chauhan got one last chance. Many accused excused for that day; jailed accused produced by video link. Next date 18 January 2025.
plain.125: Order of 3 December 2024. Accused Megha Chauhan (Tak), No. 163, filed an application asking for her passport back and for permission to travel to South Korea. The court had it registered as a separate application and issued notice to SFIO for its response on 10 December 2024. No decision on the travel request yet.
plain.126: Order of 13 January 2025. SFIO asked the court to declare accused Siddharth Chauhan a proclaimed person (absconding/wanted), because the High Court had dismissed his petition on 9 January 2025. The court only had the application registered and listed it with the main case on 24 January 2025; no decision yet.
plain.127: Hearing of 18 January 2025 before Judge Jagdeep Singh. Jodhpur jail did not produce Mukesh Modi, saying he was on interim bail till 1 March 2025, though neither this court nor the High Court had granted it; the court sought a detailed report from the Jodhpur jail superintendent. Siddharth Chauhan's High Court petition was withdrawn on 9 January 2025; he cited treatment at Fortis Hospital, Gurugram, and was given 30 days, until 27 February 2025, to appear or face being declared absconding. Neha Ghemawat and Meenakshi Modi relied on Supreme Court protection from arrest, but were told to show a court-attendance stay or appear, failing which coercive steps.
plain.128: Hearing of 27 February 2025 before Judge Jagdeep Singh. Siddharth Chauhan sought to be excused, but his anticipatory bail petition had been withdrawn in the High Court on 25 February 2025; the court rejected his request and ordered him to appear by 7 April 2025 under the earlier public proclamation, or face consequences. Neha Ghemawat and Meenakshi Modi again neither appeared nor produced any Rajasthan High Court order; the judge agreed their bond application was not maintainable while they defy the court, issued fresh summons and warned of coercive steps, as the case is stalled by three absent accused. Jodhpur jail still had not explained Mukesh Modi's supposed interim bail.
plain.129: Order dated 3 April 2025: no one present. The judge, Jagdeep Singh, was going to be on casual leave from 4 to 7 April 2025 (6 April being a Sunday), so the case was simply adjourned to 3 May 2025 for the same purpose, with all concerned to be informed. Routine adjournment only.
plain.130: Order dated 2 May 2025: no one present. Because the judge, Jagdeep Singh, was going to be on casual leave on 3 May 2025, the case was simply adjourned to 31 May 2025 for the purpose already fixed, and all concerned were to be informed of the new date. Routine adjournment only; nothing else decided.
plain.131: Order dated 29 May 2025: no one present. The judge, Jagdeep Singh, would be on casual leave on 31 May 2025, so the case was simply adjourned to 22 July 2025 for the purpose already fixed, and everyone concerned was to be informed. Routine adjournment only; nothing else was decided that day.
plain.132: Hearing of 19 September 2025 before Judge Jagdeep Singh. Jodhpur jail had released Mukesh Modi claiming interim bail, though he has no bail in this case; the court said the jail superintendent appeared to be helping him unlawfully and sought a report from Rajasthan's Home Secretary by 6 November 2025, warning of a contempt reference. Non-bailable arrest warrants against 14 accused, including Nitin Rathore, Abhay K. Shah, Aditya Sarda, Nazima and Shabbir Khan, came back unexecuted and were reissued; the Khans' plea to pause was refused for lack of a stay. Siddharth Chauhan cited a Supreme Court stay but did not appear. Jainam Rathod is jailed in Sabarmati, Ahmedabad.
plain.133: Hearing of 6 November 2025 after transfer to Judge Gagan Geet Kaur. Jodhpur jail reported Mukesh Modi was freed on medical interim bail by the Rajasthan High Court, though his bail here is pending in the Punjab and Haryana High Court; he did not appear, so the court reported this to the High Court. Excuses for absence (fever, back pain, eye injury, Mumbai seminar; Meenakshi Modi caring for husband Mukesh Modi after knee surgery; Neha Ghemawat's spine surgery advice) allowed for that day only, proof required. Pleas by Aditya Sarda, Nazima and Shabbir Khan to pause the case rejected without a stay; arrest warrants reissued as homes were locked.
plain.134: Hearing of 7 January 2026 before Judge Gagan Geet Kaur. Mukesh Modi and Rahul Modi, freed from Jodhpur jail on Rajasthan High Court interim bail although the Punjab and Haryana High Court dismissed their bail here on 22 December 2025, sought medical excuse; refused, bail bonds forfeited, arrest warrants issued, medical papers to be verified, AIIMS Delhi check-up ordered. Meenakshi Modi (caring for husband) and Rohit Modi (caring for wife after surgery) also refused, bonds forfeited, arrest warrants issued. SFIO asked that Shiv Raj Sharma be accepted as approver. Warrants against 14 others postponed over a Supreme Court no-coercive-action order. Siddharth Chauhan's surrender-and-bail plea rejected as he was absent.
plain.135: Order of 20 February 2026 before Judge Puneet Sehgal, after the case was transferred to him. Accused Megha Chauhan (No. 163) had applied to get her passport back from the court so she could apply for a US visa. Arguments on her request were not heard that day and it was adjourned to 25 February 2026 for consideration. No decision yet.
plain.136: Order of 20 February 2026 before Judge Puneet Sehgal, after transfer of the case. Accused Indu Tak (No. 164) had applied for release of her passport held by the court so she could apply for a US visa. Arguments were not heard that day; the request was adjourned to 25 February 2026 for consideration. No decision yet.
plain.137: Order of 25 February 2026 before Judge Puneet Sehgal. The Supreme Court had on 17 February 2026 given accused Siddharth (Chauhan) a final extension to surrender by 20 February 2026, failing which police could act. The court clerk reported he had not surrendered despite this, so the court issued a non-bailable arrest warrant to bring him before court on 18 March.
plain.138: Short record of 25 February 2026. The lawyer for accused Indu Tak (No. 164), Neeraj Dev Gaur, stated that he was withdrawing her application for return of her passport (sought for a US visa) because it had become pointless (infructuous), keeping the right to file a fresh one later. The withdrawal was recorded.
plain.139: Hearing of 18 March 2026 before Judge Puneet Sehgal. The court accepted accused Shiv Raj Sharma as an approver, meaning he is pardoned and will switch sides to testify for the prosecution, based on his application, the High Court's bail order and his sworn statements. SFIO was told to file an amended case title showing pardoned persons as prosecution witnesses. The arrest warrant against Siddharth Chauhan came back unserved, so a fresh non-bailable warrant was issued for 17 April 2026. Mukesh Modi and Rahul Modi were not produced from Jodhpur; production warrants issued. Six accused excused for that day.
plain.140: Order of 17 April 2026 refusing accused Indu Tak (No. 164) permission to travel to Vietnam from 7 to 18 May 2026 and return of her passport. She said she was on anticipatory bail since 2020, had travelled to Malaysia and Singapore in October 2023 and returned on time. SFIO opposed, citing serious financial-fraud charges under the Companies Act and cheating, and said she was a flight risk. The judge dismissed the request because she did not state any purpose for the Vietnam trip, which he found to be deliberately concealed.
plain.141: Hearing of 17 April 2026 before Judge Puneet Sehgal. Siddharth Chauhan ignored the Supreme Court's final deadline to surrender by 20 February 2026 and arrest warrants came back unexecuted. His lawyer offered bail bonds and to deposit the alleged amount, but the unsigned application was rejected as he was absent and there was no stay; the court revived and confirmed his status as a proclaimed offender (declared absconding). Following the High Court's 22 December 2025 order, SFIO must list who has and has not appeared, so the trial of absent accused can be separated. Eleven absent accused summoned by bailable warrants of Rs 10,000.
plain.142: Order dated 30 May 2026 before Judge Yashwinder Paul Singh: no one present. Because the judge was going on summer vacation from 1 to 15 June 2026, the case was simply adjourned to 10 July 2026 for the purpose already fixed, and all concerned were to be informed. Routine adjournment only.
plain.143: Hearing of 10 July 2026 before Judge Yashwinder Paul Singh, recorded as a full attendance table of all 187 accused and companies. The court noted that ten accused, including Ajit Singh Rathore, Ramlal Arya, Damyanti Bhandari and Shashank Shekhar Singh Rathore, had become approvers (prosecution witnesses) in 2024 and need not attend. The main case file was not put before the court, so the court clerk was told to trace it and be careful in future. Fifteen accused were excused for the day; court notices issued to absent accused, including Mukesh Modi and Rahul Modi. The table marks Siddharth Chauhan as present. Next date 29 July 2026.
plain.144: Hearing of 29 July 2026 before Judge Yashwinder Paul Singh, mainly an attendance table of all 187 accused. Twelve accused, including Neha Ghemawat, Siddharth Chauhan, Shiv Raj Sharma, Megha Chauhan and Indu Tak, were excused from coming that day. The judge noted the court clerk had not arranged the case file properly, so with 187 accused and the case still at the stage of summoning the accused, the true position of each accused could not be worked out; the SFIO prosecutor was told to help the court on the summoning status of every accused next time. Adjourned to 19 August 2026.
plain.145: Hearing of 19 August 2026 before Judge Yashwinder Paul Singh. SFIO filed an amended list of parties. Aditya Sarda's address was corrected to 3 Alipore Park Place, Kolkata, and SFIO agreed to give him all case documents on a pen drive. He also filed a Supreme Court order of 14 July 2026 directing the trial court to frame charges, allowing it to issue non-bailable arrest warrants to secure accused, and calling for a status report after three months. Nine accused excused for the day. Rajeshwar Singh, Bharat Modi, Ishwar Singh Sindal and Bharat Das Vaishnav, held in Jodhpur Central Jail in other cases, to be produced on 25 August 2026.
plain.146: Hearing of 25 August 2026 before Judge Yashwinder Paul Singh. Mukesh Modi and Rahul Virendra Modi, wrongly released from Jodhpur jail without bail in this case, were found to be evading court, so the court ordered them declared wanted by public proclamation: read out and pasted at their homes and the court, and published in a newspaper at SFIO's cost, requiring them to appear on 8 October 2026. Non-bailable arrest warrants were issued for Bharat Modi (released from Jodhpur jail but absent), Bharat Das Vaishnav and Rajiv Kumar Rana, whose Supreme Court bail can be cancelled if he skips court.
plain.147: Short order of 31 August 2026. The SFIO's court clerk (perokar) and Special Public Prosecutor came, and the proclamation papers declaring accused Mukesh Modi (113) and Rahul Virendra Modi (114) wanted/absconding were handed to them for putting up publicly. The case was listed on 7 September 2026 to record their statements about carrying out the proclamation.
plain.148: Short order of 7 September 2026. The SFIO clerk did not turn up, so the prosecutor got a date of 8 September 2026 to record statements on how the public proclamation against Mukesh Modi and Rahul Virendra Modi was carried out. The judge found the court clerk (Ahlmad) had failed to issue the non-bailable arrest warrants ordered against Bharat Modi and Bharat Vaishnav, and warned him to be careful. The prosecutor sought time to check their status.
plain.149: Order of 8 September 2026 recording how the public proclamation declaring Mukesh Modi and Rahul Virendra Modi wanted was carried out. SFIO Assistant Director Yashika Sharma handed the papers to law consultant Sandeep Kumar Yadav, who read them aloud and pasted them at Gurugram's new court building on 3 September 2026, then flew to Udaipur and went by taxi to their last known address, A-10 Adarsh Nagar, Sirohi, Rajasthan, pasting them on the boundary wall and announcing them in the main market. Their appearance stays fixed for 8 October 2026. Bharat Modi, possibly in Jodhpur jail, to be produced; fresh arrest warrant for Bharat Vaishnav via DCP (HQ).
